'''''Nidularium''''' is a [[genus]] in the plant [[Family (taxonomy)|family]] [[Bromeliaceae]], subfamily [[Bromelioideae]]. Named to describe the nestling characteristic of the [[inflorescence]] (Lat. nidulus = little nest), all the species are [[Endemism|endemic]] to Brazil.<ref name=q>[http://apps.kew.org/wcsp/namedetail.do?name_id=255522 Kew World Checklist of Selected Plant Families]</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Martinelli |first1=Gustavo |last2=Vieira |first2=Cláudia Magalhães |last3=Gonzalez |first3=Marcos |last4=Leitman |first4=Paula |last5=Piratininga |first5=Andréa |last6=Costa |first6=Andrea Ferreira da |last7=Forzza |first7=Rafaela Campostrini |title=Bromeliaceae da Mata Atlântica Brasileira: lista de espécies, distribuição e conservação |journal=Rodriguésia |date=January 2008 |volume=59 |issue=1 |pages=209–258 |doi=10.1590/2175-7860200859114 |trans-title=Bromeliaceae of the brazilian Atlantic Forest: checklist, distribution and conservation |language=pt-BR|doi-access=free }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Monteiro |first1=R.F. |last2=Moreira |first2=B.A. |title=''Nidularium'' |url=http://floradobrasil.jbrj.gov.br/reflora/floradobrasil/FB6229 |website=Flora do Brasil 2020 |publisher=Jardim Botânico do Rio de Janeiro}}</ref> Commonly confused with ''[[Neoregelia]]'' which they resemble, this plant group was first described in 1854.<ref>Lemaire, (Antoine) Charles. 1854.  Jardin Fleuriste 4: t. 411, Misc. 60</ref>
